objects.title: Geometry Projection Operator
objects.formal_definition: Pi_geo : Topology_app -> Geometry_app, admissible only when four mandatory invariants survive projection
objects.operator_note: Pi_geo is NOT a geometry-producing theorem. It is a legality-conditioned routing operator. Geometry_app is reachable only if distinction, admissibility, orientation-trace, and closure-trace all survive the mapping.
mandatory_invariant_checks: orientation_trace: orientation class remains recoverable after projection
closure_trace: closure identity remains traceable after projection

objects.title: Geometry-to-Topology Projection Trace Map
objects.formal_definition: tau_geo : Geometry_app -> Topology_app_trace, a partial inverse-style trace map used to verify that required invariant labels of a topological state T survive projection under Pi_geo
objects.operator_note: tau_geo is NOT a full inverse of Pi_geo. It is a recoverability check: tau_geo(Pi_geo(T)) must retain the required invariant labels (orientation class, closure identity) of the original T for the projection to be considered legal. If tau_geo fails to recover any required label, Pi_geo is inadmissible for that class of inputs.

recoverability_obligations.check: tau_geo(Pi_geo(T)) retains orientation class label of T
tau_geo(Pi_geo(T)) retains closure identity label of T; tau_geo is injective w.r.t. closure equivalence classes

objects.title: Topology-to-Geometry Admissible Projection Legality Gap
objects.gap_reclassification_note: Gap reclassified by GEO_GAP_REDUCTION_SEQUENCE_001. The gap is NOT missing geometry; it is missing proof that Pi_geo is a legally admissible projection. Geometry_app cannot be promoted until all four invariant preservation checks pass and GEO_PROJECTION_VALIDATION_001 runs with full control battery.
objects.bridge_routing_note: OPEN_BRIDGE_001 may constrain topological selection (selector-form) but does NOT provide promotion support for Geometry_app. Its role here is structural routing only.

objects.title: RT Mechanics as Recursive Relational Completion
Org_a
objects.definition: Define Org_a as admissible organization over distinction-generating participation fields, using vertical-bar closure, grouped-bar closure, and orientation preservation as explicit prerequisites.
objects.relationship_to_D: Org_a does not create distinction from nothing; it organizes already evaluable admissible distinction participation.
objects.relationship_to_iff_R: iff_R supplies the admissible preservation relation under which Org_a transformations are judged.
objects.relationship_to_orientation: Org_a must preserve admissible orientation structure across legal transformations.
objects.relationship_to_Sigma_D: Sigma_D can now be drafted as an equivalence class or signature of Org_a-closed distinction organizations.

objects.title: Sigma_D
objects.definition: Define Sigma_D admissible equivalence criteria using Org_a closure, iff_R preservation, and orientation equivalence.

equivalence_rules.Sigma_D_equivalence: Σ_D(G) = Σ_D(G') iff G and G' preserve the same Org_a-closed distinction organization under iff_R and orientation equivalence ≃_O.

objects.relationship_to_Org_a: Org_a defines admissible organization closure; Sigma_D defines equivalence of such closed organizations.

objects.title: vertical_bar_operator
objects.definition: The vertical bar operator compares one process-aspect to another while preserving non-collapse sufficient for distinction generation.
objects.reading: A compared to B under preserved distinction.

valid_operands: domain-specific projections explicitly typed as admissible operands
invalid_operands: pure scalar quantities without participation type
semantic placeholders with no admissibility trace

orientation_rules.orientation_statement: A | B is not generally equivalent to B | A.

closure_rules.local_closure: A bar expression is locally closed when both operands are admissibly typed and the comparison relation is legally evaluable under D.
closure_rules.grouped_closure: Grouped bar expressions require a separate group-closure rule.

objects.same_process_constraint_note: Distinction generated through | is governed as deviated constraint within the same process, not as a separate residue object.

formal_candidate.reading: A compared to B without collapse under declared context C.
formal_candidate.Compare_C_note: Compare_C is the minimal declared comparison context licensing D_C to evaluate. It is not a state container or memory object.
formal_candidate.TS0_status: formal_candidate — no evidence yet; campaign design required before promotion

objects.title: orientation_space_O
objects.definition: Define Orientation Space O as the admissible space of participation directions governing bar expressions, Org_a preservation, and knot-class selection.
objects.orientation_equivalence: G ≃_O G' iff there exist o ∈ O(G), o' ∈ O(G') such that participation directions, roles, and closure are preserved under iff_R.
objects.relationship_to_bar_operator: A|B carries orientation by default. Binary case O(A|B) and group case O(G) record the legal participation direction.
objects.relationship_to_Org_a: Org_a must preserve admissible orientation structure across legal transformations.
objects.relationship_to_OPEN_BRIDGE_001: Orientation functions as a topological selector constraint on admissible knot-class selection.

group_operand_rules.operand_requirement: Every participant A_i must satisfy Typed_a(A_i) or be explicitly marked as pending admissibility qualification.
group_operand_rules.interface_requirement: Every adjacent or declared interface A_i | A_j must be legally evaluable under D or a registered successor evaluator.

associativity_rules.statement: (A|B)|C is not automatically equivalent to A|(B|C).

permutation_rules.statement: A|B|C is not automatically equivalent to B|A|C, A|C|B, or any other permutation.

objects.title: Re_orientation_Trigger_Condition
objects.canonical_form: Trigger_Reorient(x,c,R_↔,C_t,C_t^S) = TRUE iff [δ_a(x;c)=∅] OR [C_t^S=∅] OR [S_closure < τ_R] OR [Def_a(x,c) requires new -(i)]
objects.formal_definition: A control rule that diverts the continuation pipeline into orientation reassessment when the current orientation regime cannot sustain admissible continuation.
objects.non_promotion_note: This control rule manages pre-realization orientation triggers only. It does not select realized continuation q* and does not promote topology, geometry, or physics-app claims.

objects.title: Primitive Affect/Effect Distinction Condition
objects.formal_definition: The primitive affect/effect distinction condition within the affect/effect domain. It is distinct from A_meta/B_meta and must not be substituted into RT_core bindings.

objects.title: Distinction Projection Operator
objects.formal_definition: A projection operator that maps the primitive affect/effect distinction condition into the representational distinction schema D(*|*).

objects.title: Formal Distinction Projection
objects.formal_definition: The representational distinction projection of A|E. It is not primitive and remains domain-local to the affect/effect projection layer.

objects.title: Residue-Governed Continuation Arrow
objects.formal_definition: A ->r B denotes the continuation object C(A,B), the lawful process relating condition A to condition B under residue-governed admissibility; it is not a syntactic rewrite operator.

objects.title: Residue Continuation Constraint
objects.formal_definition: The historical residue condition that constrains admissible continuation from A into B.

objects.title: Continuation Object
objects.formal_definition: A first-class lawful process object relating condition A to condition B under residue-governed admissibility; A ->r B denotes this continuation object, and A and B are its stabilized endpoints.

objects.title: Continuation Composition
objects.formal_definition: Lawful process composition of continuation objects that yields C(A,C) only when the shared endpoint matches and residue/admissibility are preserved; the operation is process composition, not symbolic concatenation or rewrite.

objects.title: Identity Continuation
objects.formal_definition: The lawful continuation that preserves condition A without changing its semantic state; it is the neutral element of continuation composition and is not a static state.

objects.title: Process Equivalence
objects.formal_definition: A binary process-equivalence relation on continuation expressions that holds when they produce the same admissible continuation behavior under the same governing conditions; it is not mere symbolic equality.

objects.title: Canonical Continuation Form
objects.formal_definition: The canonical representative of a continuation expression when admissibility holds; it supports auditability and comparison without specifying the reduction algorithm.

objects.title: Continuation Reduction Semantics
objects.formal_definition: A governed reduction relation that transforms a well-formed continuation expression toward its canonical continuation form NF(C) while preserving process equivalence and leaving RT_core unchanged; it is not a symbolic rewrite operator.

objects.title: Primitive Continuation Reduction Rules
objects.canonical_form: I(A) ∘ C(A,B) ->red C(A,B); C(A,B) ∘ I(B) ->red C(A,B); C(A,B) ∘ C(B,C) ->red C(A,C)
objects.formal_definition: The first concrete lawful reduction rules under continuation reduction semantics. The rules remove identity redundancy and contract lawful composition toward NF(C) only when endpoint compatibility, admissibility, residue propagation, and governing constraints hold.

objects.title: Well-Formed Continuation Expression
objects.formal_definition: A continuation expression whose endpoints, composition structure, domain bindings, and governing constraints are valid; reduction and composition are lawful only when the expression is well-formed.

objects.title: Typed Continuation Domains
objects.canonical_form: type(A_meta) = TYPE_META; type(A|E) = TYPE_AFFECT_EFFECT; type(Π_D(A|E)) = TYPE_PROJECTION; type(D(*|*)) = TYPE_PROJECTION; type(C(A,B)) = TYPE_CONTINUATION; type(NF(C)) = TYPE_CONTINUATION; type(Obs(A_affect,B_affect)) = TYPE_OBSERVATION; type(RT_operational_regime) = TYPE_OPERATIONAL_REGIME
objects.formal_definition: Explicit domain typing constraints for continuation expressions across meta, affect/effect, projection, continuation, observation, and operational-regime layers. Domain compatibility is required for lawful continuation composition and reduction; cross-domain substitution requires explicit projection, binding, or transition rule.

objects.title: Typed Projection Transition Rules
objects.formal_definition: A typed transition relation from the primitive affect/effect condition into the projection layer, licensed only by explicit invocation of Π_D. Direct collapse from A|E to D(*|*) is forbidden, and the projection preserves representable distinction without exhausting the primitive condition.

objects.title: Typed Continuation Composition Guards
objects.canonical_form: cod(C(A,B)) = dom(C(B,C)); type(cod(C1)) = type(dom(C2)) or explicit typed transition rule exists; admissible(C1,C2); residue propagation preserved; C(A,B) ∘ C(B,C) ->red C(A,C) only after typed composition guards pass
objects.formal_definition: Typed continuation composition guards require endpoint matching, typed-domain compatibility, admissibility, and residue propagation before composition or any composed reduction is lawful. Projection-domain mismatches require an explicit typed transition rule such as Π_D; failed composition produces no continuation object.

objects.title: Continuation Failure
objects.canonical_form: Compose(C1,C2) = ⊥C on endpoint, type, admissibility, or residue failure; Reduce(C) = ⊥C on guard failure; NF(⊥C) undefined
objects.formal_definition: Marked diagnostic failure state produced when a proposed continuation cannot be admitted as a lawful continuation object. Continuation failure records inadmissibility without modifying RT_core and must not be reduced into NF(C).

objects.title: Continuation Failure Classification
objects.canonical_form: ⊥C_endpoint, ⊥C_type, ⊥C_adm, and ⊥C_res refine ⊥C diagnostically; Recover(⊥C_x) and NF(⊥C_x) remain undefined in this patch
objects.formal_definition: Diagnostic classification of continuation failure into endpoint, type, admissibility, and residue subclasses. Classification records why continuation failed but does not create a lawful continuation object or any recovery semantics.

objects.title: Continuation Expression Evaluation Order
objects.canonical_form: parse expression; check WF(C); check domain types; apply explicit typed transitions; check endpoint compatibility; check admissibility; check residue propagation; classify failure if checks fail; permit composition if checks pass; permit reduction toward NF(C)
objects.formal_definition: Ordered evaluation pipeline for continuation expressions. Evaluation is gated by well-formedness, typing, typed transitions, endpoint compatibility, admissibility, and residue propagation before composition or reduction is admitted.

objects.title: Minimal Continuation Reduction Algorithm
objects.canonical_form: EVAL_024; if guard failure -> ⊥C_x; apply identity reduction; contract lawful composition to C(A,C); repeat while ≡P is preserved; return NF(C) or partial_NF(C)
algorithm_steps: If any guard fails, return classified ⊥C_x.
If expression contains identity composition, apply identity reduction.
If expression contains lawful composed continuation C(A,B) ∘ C(B,C), reduce to C(A,C).
Repeat lawful reductions while process equivalence is preserved.
Return NF(C) if no further lawful reductions are available.
If normalization cannot be completed, return partial_NF(C) with unresolved status.
objects.formal_definition: Minimal governed reduction procedure for well-formed continuation expressions after EVAL_024 admits composition and reduction. It returns classified ⊥C_x on guard failure, preserves process equivalence on every lawful step, and may return partial_NF(C) when full normalization is unresolved. Termination and confluence are not asserted.

objects.title: Partial Normal Form
objects.canonical_form: WF(C) and Typed(C) and no continuation failure; reduction has halted at the current calculus boundary while additional lawful reductions remain outside the executable boundary
objects.formal_definition: Admissible, type-correct continuation expression whose lawful reductions are incomplete because the current calculus boundary does not yet admit the remaining lawful reductions. The 025 surface label partial_NF(C) denotes this state.

objects.title: Reduction Outcome Classification
objects.formal_definition: Canonical classifier that maps REDUCE_025 outputs into NF(C), pNF(C), or continuation failure. The legacy partial_NF(C) surface is classified as pNF(C).

objects.title: Reduction Trace
objects.formal_definition: Canonical diagnostic record of the evaluation, validation, lawful reduction, halt, and failure-classification sequence applied to a continuation expression by REDUCE_025. Trace(C) records the realized sequence for NF(C), pNF(C), or classified continuation failure and does not modify reduction semantics.

objects.title: Trace Step
objects.canonical_form: τ_i := single ordered trace event with pre_state, post_state, rule_applied, admissibility_status, residue_status, and failure_class
objects.formal_definition: Single evaluation, validation, reduction, halt, or failure-classification event within Trace(C). Trace steps are the atomic members of the ordered reduction trace and do not alter reduction semantics.

objects.title: Reduction Trace Equivalence
objects.formal_definition: An equivalence relation over reduction traces that holds when two traces originate from the same input continuation, preserve lawful reduction semantics, preserve process-equivalent continuation behavior, terminate in the same canonical outcome, and preserve halt classification. It is diagnostic only and does not modify reduction semantics.

objects.title: Canonical Trace Form
objects.canonical_form: TNF(Trace) := normalized trace representative with canonical reduction events, normalized step numbering, and normalized halt classification
objects.formal_definition: Normalized representative of a reduction trace used for equivalence comparison. TNF(Trace) preserves evaluation order, removes implementation-specific metadata, retains canonical reduction events, and normalizes step numbering and halt classification without altering reduction semantics.

objects.title: Local Confluence
objects.formal_definition: A bounded reduction property stating that two lawful reductions diverging from the same continuation may be reduced to process-equivalent continuation outcomes under the current reduction system. It is local only and does not assert global confluence.

objects.title: Reduction Branch
objects.canonical_form: Branch(C) := lawful reduction path from a common continuation expression
objects.formal_definition: A lawful reduction path originating from a common continuation expression.

objects.title: Joinability
objects.formal_definition: A relation indicating that two lawful reduction branches can be reduced to process-equivalent continuation outcomes.

objects.title: Critical Reduction Pair
objects.formal_definition: A pair of immediately divergent lawful reductions originating from the same continuation requiring local confluence evaluation.

objects.title: Reduction Determinism
objects.canonical_form: Det(C) := unique lawful reduction outcome under canonical evaluation order and reduction priority
objects.formal_definition: A property indicating that a continuation expression has a unique lawful reduction outcome under the canonical evaluation order and reduction priority.

objects.title: Reduction Priority
objects.canonical_form: Priority(R) := canonical ordering for simultaneously admissible lawful reductions
objects.formal_definition: The canonical ordering used when multiple lawful reductions are simultaneously admissible.

objects.title: Reduction Choice Function
objects.canonical_form: Choose(C) := deterministic selection of the next lawful reduction by canonical reduction priority
objects.formal_definition: The deterministic selection function that chooses the next lawful reduction according to canonical reduction priority.

objects.title: Deterministic Continuation Class
objects.formal_definition: The class of continuation expressions satisfying the bounded determinism conditions.

objects.title: Termination
objects.canonical_form: Term(C) := finite lawful reduction sequence to a reduction outcome
objects.formal_definition: A property indicating that REDUCE_025 reaches a reduction outcome after a finite number of lawful reduction steps.

objects.title: Reduction Measure
objects.canonical_form: μ(C) := well-founded reduction measure used to evaluate reduction progress
objects.formal_definition: A well-founded measure used to evaluate reduction progress.

objects.title: Reduction Progress
objects.formal_definition: Each lawful reduction strictly decreases the reduction measure.

objects.title: Termination Class
objects.formal_definition: Classification of continuation expressions according to bounded termination behavior.

objects.title: Canonical Form Uniqueness
objects.canonical_form: Unique(C) := unique canonical normal form modulo process equivalence
objects.formal_definition: A property indicating that a continuation possesses a unique canonical normal form modulo process equivalence.

objects.title: Canonical Representative
objects.canonical_form: Rep(C) := canonical representative selected after lawful reduction
objects.formal_definition: The selected representative of a process-equivalence class after lawful reduction.

objects.title: Normal Form Equivalence Class
objects.formal_definition: The equivalence class of all canonical normal forms related by process equivalence.

objects.title: Uniqueness Class
objects.formal_definition: Classification of continuation expressions according to bounded canonical-form uniqueness.

objects.title: Reduction Complexity
objects.canonical_form: κ(C) := abstract reduction complexity independent of implementation, runtime, and syntax size
objects.formal_definition: An abstract measure of the intrinsic reduction complexity of a continuation expression under the RT Calculus.

objects.title: Complexity Delta
objects.formal_definition: The change in reduction complexity produced by a lawful reduction step.

objects.title: Reduction Cost
objects.canonical_form: Cost(C) := accumulated abstract reduction complexity required to reach a terminal outcome
objects.formal_definition: The accumulated reduction complexity required to reach a terminal reduction outcome.

objects.title: Reduction Complexity Class
objects.canonical_form: Classκ := {C | κ(C) is classified as Minimal, Reducible, Undetermined, or Failure}
objects.formal_definition: Classification of continuation expressions according to abstract reduction complexity.

objects.title: Bounded Confluence Theorem
objects.canonical_form: Conf_B(C) := bounded confluence over an admissible bounded continuation class
objects.formal_definition: The property that all lawful reduction branches belonging to an admissible bounded continuation class converge to process-equivalent canonical outcomes.

objects.title: Confluence Class
objects.formal_definition: A continuation class satisfying all bounded confluence prerequisites.

objects.title: Canonical Reduction Strategy
objects.canonical_form: S(C) := canonical reduction strategy governing lawful selection among admissible reduction candidates
objects.formal_definition: The canonical strategy governing lawful reduction selection whenever multiple admissible reduction candidates exist.

objects.title: Reduction Candidate Set
objects.canonical_form: Cand(C) := {r | r is a lawful reduction candidate after EVAL_024}
objects.formal_definition: The complete set of lawful reduction candidates available after EVAL_024.

objects.title: Strategy Ordering
objects.canonical_form: ≺S := canonical ordering relation over lawful reduction candidates
objects.formal_definition: The canonical ordering relation used to rank lawful reduction candidates.

objects.title: Strategy Class
objects.canonical_form: ClassS := {C | S(C) is applicable within the bounded deterministic class}
objects.formal_definition: Classification of continuation expressions according to canonical strategy applicability.

objects.title: Canonical Reduction Strategy Correctness
objects.canonical_form: Correct(S) := bounded correctness of the canonical reduction strategy
objects.formal_definition: The property that the canonical reduction strategy preserves lawful reduction semantics for bounded continuation classes.

objects.title: Correctness Class
objects.formal_definition: Continuation classes satisfying all bounded correctness prerequisites.
